summary: The Spaceship is the protagonist's primary mode of transportation, built by Slate. It is a single-pilot craft with two multi-directional thruster banks, an on-board computer, Signalscope and Scout Launcher, Nomai artificial gravity, and modular hull sections that can take and report damage.

behavior: The Spaceship has room for exactly one pilot.
The Spaceship is entered from the bottom via a circular hatch.
When the hatch is open, it emits a beam of blue light that tugs the player upward to allow re-entry.
The hatch closes automatically once the player enters.
When the hatch is opened from outside, a salvaged Nomai gravity ring activates and lifts the player inside.
location: The Spaceship is parked at the Launch Tower on Timber Hearth at the start of every loop.
The Spaceship is divided into a central hull, aft hull, starboard hull, port hull, and cockpit.
lore: The Spaceship was built by Slate.
The Spaceship's on-board computer is a fixed version of the power source seen at the Observatory.
The aft hull contains the Computer, a poster of the solar system, supplies, and a hatchet.
The starboard hull holds the spacesuit hanger and emergency supplies cabinet.
The port hull contains the Generator and a gravity crystal.
Both the Generator and the port-hull gravity crystal can be repaired from inside the ship.
mechanics: The ship is propelled by two banks of multi-directional thrusters, allowing motion in any direction.
Each thruster bank has five nozzles, one for each axis except the mounting point.
When one thruster bank is broken, the ship becomes nearly uncontrollable due to asymmetric thrust but is still flyable.
Ship parts and subsystems take localized damage from high-velocity impacts; sections start losing health at impacts of about 30 m/s or more.
If a hull section's health drops below 30%, a flashing red light and alarm activate until repairs are complete.
Port and starboard hull at 0% health detach from the ship, rendering it inoperable.
Landing gear starts taking damage only above ~80 m/s impacts.
When landing gear reaches 0%, one of three legs detaches and the ship lands unevenly.
Repairing landing gear restores texture but does not bring back a detached leg.
Repairs can only be performed from outside the ship except for the Generator and gravity crystal subsystems inside.
The cockpit can be ejected with a button protected by a glass panel, breaching the hull at 50 m/s and granting an Achievement.
Ejecting the cockpit destroys the ship's electric systems but the player remains in the seat.
The on-board Computer provides info on visited planets and includes a 'Theory mode' for connecting clues.
The Computer allows marking specific locations on the HUD for easier relocation.
Autopilot accelerates straight at a selected celestial body for half the distance, then decelerates, stopping just before the body.
Autopilot does not avoid obstacles; an inattentive pilot can fly into the sun or planets.
If the player tries to leave the solar system, autopilot automatically retargets the sun, unless autopilot is broken or disabled.
Autopilot can be disabled in the options for increased difficulty or to fly outside the solar system.
Match Velocity (A on controller) reduces relative velocity to zero but does not match orbit.
Three indicator lights in the cockpit show system state: white for headlight, green for autopilot, orange for velocity matching.
The temperature gauge in the cockpit is non-functional and not implemented in the game.
The ship-mounted Signalscope works like the player's but cannot tune to unknown frequencies or zoom in.
Landing mode shows a low-resolution black-and-white camera feed of the surface below, with a navball and altimeter.
Landing mode automatically rotates the ship's underside toward the targeted body until disabled.
The ship-mounted Scout Launcher launches the Scout at much higher speed than the player's portable launcher.
When the electrical system is broken, the headlight, landing cam, computer, and inside lighting all stop working.
When the oxygen tank is broken, it leaks and empties in about 20 minutes; however, the ship still retains infinite oxygen even after the tank is empty.
When the fuel tank is broken, fuel runs out in about a minute; repairs stop the leak but do not refund lost fuel.
Match Velocity remains usable even with no fuel.
Artificial gravity inside the ship is provided by a Nomai gravity crystal and produces about 0.8x normal acceleration.
Unlike other Nomai gravity crystals, the ship's gravity adds to outside forces rather than erasing them.
On Giant's Deep, a player inside the ship feels about 2.9x normal gravity (rather than 2.0x at sea level).
When the ship's gravity crystal is broken, the player experiences outside forces directly, including acceleration during autopilot.
When the reactor is broken, it overheats and explodes in about 20 seconds if not repaired.
A reactor explosion violently breaks apart hull sections and landing legs and propels them outward.
